correctness.rationale: For any nontrivial STS the extension spectrum of a three-point tuple depends only on its equality and block diagram, implying the common rank-four theory. In binary projective systems of dimension at least four, the first four moves preserve a linear-span isomorphism, and on the fifth the only nongeneric fresh points are at most six pair sums; a matching generic exists among at least 15 points. In ternary affine systems of dimension at least three, the same argument uses affine-span isomorphisms and pair completions, with at least 27 points. The two explicitly written quantifier-rank-five formulas detect, independently, a Pasch configuration and a four-cap without opposite-pair completion coincidences, giving the four truth vectors (1,0),(1,1),(0,0),(0,1). The 7,15,9,27-point representatives are therefore minimal. The packaged verifier separately computes exact orbit-reduced Hintikka types at ranks 0–5 in six cases and verifies the finite formula values. No finite enumeration is used to establish unbounded dimension stabilization.

originality.rationale: The fully examined classification of additive Steiner triple systems gives the two algebraic families but not a quantifier-rank-five classification, explicit rank-five formulas, or the first dimension cutoff in each family. The model-theory preprint investigates the infinite generic Steiner quasigroup and model completion, and the configuration papers analyze Pasch/anti-Pasch existence and enumeration rather than finite first-order depth. The previously known rank-four agreement is strictly weaker than this complete four-class rank-five statement. Comparison of mathematical implications with accessible primary literature and targeted indexed records uncovered no dominating theorem. Potential overlap in inaccessible or unindexed articles is a stated residual risk, not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: Two closely related historical anti-Pasch sources were not available as full text during this review.
Equivalent rank-five logical classifications could be present in unindexed literature or in treatments phrased in a dual/incidence language.
The chosen point-only relational language is essential; equivalence in a functional Steiner quasigroup signature is different.

value.rationale: The complete rank-five invariant is attached to the full, mathematically natural family of nontrivial finite additive Steiner triple systems, rather than arbitrary moduli or a selected finite slice. It determines the first logical depth that separates any two such systems, identifies two independent configuration tests that recover the characteristic and first dimension transition, and supplies sharp minimal representatives 7,9,15,27. This is information absent from the underlying algebraic isomorphism classification and has immediate use for finite bounded-depth equivalence tests. The Pasch and cap configurations are standard, but the complete logical classification is not merely their restatement.
